title: Keeping the route from the door to the till clear
target: A layout guide for Supermarket Simulator that follows the route a customer takes: the entrance, the walkable ground the game prepares, the fittings that stand in the way, the shelf approach and the queue at the till.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with at least one stocked shelf and a checkout
The fittings you want to place already bought
A few minutes with the shop empty enough to walk the route

steps.do: Walk the route from the door to the till before you move anything.
steps.because: the entrance is managed and can be changed, and the shop has its own prepared ground for people to walk on (EntranceManager, EntranceChangeOverlay, StoreNavmesh)

steps.do: Treat the walkable ground as one connected route, not as a set of gaps between fittings.
steps.because: the game builds a walkable ground for the shop, and a path that leaves it uses a link of its own (NavmeshBuildRegistry, OffMeshLinkNavigator)

steps.do: Place a fitting only where there is still a way past it.
steps.because: obstacles that people walk around are kept by a manager of their own, and a placement is checked before it is taken (NavMeshObstacleManager, PositionValidator)

steps.do: Line the route with the shelves you actually want reached, and keep their slots stocked.
steps.because: a shelf is a set of slots, and stock is placed into an empty slot rather than onto a general surface (RackSlot, SpawnProductOnEmptyShelf)

steps.do: Put the tills where the queue can stand without cutting the route in two.
steps.because: customers wait in a queue, the queue has positions of its own, and a checkout position can be moved (CustomerQueue, QueuePosition, MoveCheckoutPosition)

steps.do: Make the way in and the categories legible, then keep them consistent.
steps.because: the entrance has variants and a name sign, and a category sign is a placed object tied to a product category (EntranceVariantSignboard, EntranceNameSignSetter, CategorySign, ProductCategory)

steps.do: Keep delivery boxes out of the customer route while you unpack.
steps.because: a box on a shelf is tracked against a slot, and the game defines separate restock areas for boxes and vehicles (RackSlotBoxTarget, RestockAreaBoxController, VehicleRestockAreaController)

steps.do: Walk the route again after every rearrangement.
steps.because: the entrance can be changed, and the walkable ground is built again for the new layout (EntranceChangeItem, NavmeshBuildLoader)

commonMistakes: Placing a row of shelves and only then noticing there is no way past the end of it.
Leaving a delivery of boxes in the aisle while you stock the far end.
Moving a till without checking where the queue will stand.
Signing a category that is stocked somewhere else, so the sign and the shelf disagree.
Rearranging the shop while it is full and expecting the route to sort itself out.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
